Anya (Marketing): Hey runtime team — quick ask for an upcoming webinar and launch blog. We need a small-staging benchmark run that produces reproducible sample responses AND a p50/p95 latency/cost breakdown we can cite. Requirements below.

Anya (Marketing): Specs we want you to run: 
- env: small-staging (isolated, non-prod)
- model: redwood-v2-3b-q4_0 (quantized variant)
- seed: 12345 (fixed RNG seed for deterministic sampling)
- samples: 100 unique prompts (I'll drop a gist with prompts)
- warmup: 200 tokens / 200 requests warmup (whatever matches runtime)
- batch-size: 8
- metrics: token-cost, p50, p95 latency, memory peak
- trace: include per-request trace-id mapping to sample index so we can attach specific outputs to slides

Anya (Marketing): Example command we expect (feel free to adapt to runtime tool):
```
run_bench --env small-staging --model redwood-v2-3b-q4_0 --seed 12345 --samples 100 \
  --warmup 200 --batch-size 8 --measure p50,p95,cost --trace-map out/trace_map.csv
```

Anya (Marketing): Two asks: (1) confirm this is feasible in small-staging without affecting other work, and (2) can we get raw sample outputs + the metric CSVs so marketing can package the 'sample responses' for the blog.

Leo (Runtime): Ack — we can run this. Quick clarifying q's:
- do you want deterministic decoding (temp=0) or keep sampling with seed (repro on same runtime but can vary across kernels)?
- warmup granularity: 200 requests or 200 tokens? Our run_bench warmup flag is request-based by default.
- do you need KV/prefix cache prepopulation or full cold-start heatmap?

Anya (Marketing): Good Qs. We want outputs that look representative (i.e., non-zero temp). So keep temp=0.7 and top_k=40 but with the fixed RNG seed so our exact outputs reproduce on the same runtime config. Warmup should be 200 requests to let batching/KV stabilize. Also include one cold-start run (10 samples) so we can show cold vs warmed.

Leo (Runtime): Got it. We'll run with --temp 0.7 --top_k 40 --seed 12345, warmup 200 requests + separate cold-start sweep (10 samples). We'll also capture per-token cost and the runtime p50/p95. Note: quantized kernels can produce tiny nondeterminism across hosts; we'll pin to the same host image and record git sha of runtime.

Sam (Runtime): Scheduling now. ETA 36-48h. We'll attach: runtime_sha, kernel_sha, node-id, and trace_map.csv with sample_index -> trace_id -> request_id. Also output folder: s3://redwood-ci/marketing/bench/1777777777-small-staging/

deploy-bot: Job queued: bench-run-1777777777 by Sam. Status: queued -> running

Mina (Analytics): When you post CSVs, please include token counts per sample and total token cost. If possible add a column for 'warmup_completed' bool and 'cold_start' tag so analytics can compute the delta for slides.

Leo (Runtime): Will include those columns. We'll also attach a short README with the exact command + env vars used.

Anya (Marketing): Amazing — thank you. I'll post the prompt gist in this thread within the hour. Will follow up if we need a second run with alternate quantization.

Sam (Runtime): Thx — putting this on our sprint board. Will ping when artifacts are uploaded.
